title: After #36498: arrangement keys from a non-pair or non-.custom writer are only skipped at boot on three paths, not refused at a door
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmRY38EZf38Yy3zthbY

Filed as a `finding` by seat `repo:objectstack#2` from the #36498 dev report (comment 7085306548). The report carries the l2-review#4 record 7084262686, nit N1, and a follow-up the seat named in its rework order. Not triaged; not claimed. Waits on PR #36517.

## What

PR #36517 lets the paired `.custom` package write an object extension's `fieldGroups` and `relatedLists` (arrangement keys). Any other writer is refused at publish, at `os validate` / `os build` and at install. On three paths, though, a non-`.custom` writer's arrangement key is only **skipped by the registry fold with a boot-log line**, where `main` refused it at parse:

1. a code-defined stack that boots without `os validate` / `os build`;
2. a stack that names no package id: `judgeExtensionArrangement` skips a subject with no package id, so `os validate` passes it;
3. package duplicate / orphan adoption in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commits.ts`. The `__c` judge is asked there and the arrangement judge is not. Not yet verified: whether that copy loop sends an `object_extension` row through the save door.

Also, the save and install doors judge a writer by its `.custom` **suffix** only. A `.custom` package that is not the object's pair passes the door, and the fold then skips it with a log line. Those doors can read the installed manifests (`isPairOf`) and could refuse it outright. The CLI door cannot.

In every case nothing is applied, so this is not a data hazard. The gap is a declared arrangement that the platform silently ignores. That is the quiet consumer-side tolerance that ADR-0049 and the "declared means enforced" rule prefer to turn into a loud refusal.

## Ask

Make each path refuse loudly (publish / save / install / adoption), or record why a boot-time skip is the right answer there. Pin each with a test.

## Likely lane

`domain:server` (metadata-protocol, objectql), plus `domain:spec` if the parse judge moves.

## Re-check

`grep -n "judgeExtensionArrangement" -r packages/ --include=*.ts`, then confirm that a subject with no package id still returns early.
